I was particularly intrigued by her "relationship pyramid" theory, which delves into the building blocks of relationships. This theory resonated with me as I realized how essential it is to establish a solid foundation in any relationship. Priya's ability to translate complex psychological concepts into practical wisdom is truly commendable.

Moreover, she provided invaluable guidance on recognizing distinct behavior patterns in people and offered effective strategies to navigate professional interactions. Her insights have already proven beneficial in my professional environment, helping me better understand and communicate with colleagues.

Overall, my session with Priya was enlightening and transformative. Her deep understanding of human behavior, coupled with her practical advice, makes her an exceptional counselor. I am grateful for the opportunity to learn from her and would highly recommend her services to anyone seeking profound insights and effective strategies for personal and professional growth.

owner_posts.post_text:
Heel pain isn't normal and it shouldn't become part of your daily routine.
If you're struggling with plantar fasciitis, morning heel pain, foot pain, or pain while walking, this post is for you. Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain, yet many people continue living with it for months, hoping it will disappear on its own. Unfortunately, untreated plantar fasciitis often becomes chronic heel pain, making every step more uncomfortable.
Many people with plantar fasciitis choose cortisone injections because they want quick heel pain relief. Tight calf muscles, weak foot muscles, poor ankle mobility, reduced foot stability, improper footwear, prolonged standing, running overload, and walking mechanics all play a major role in persistent heel pain.

What you're seeing is Spinal Decompression Therapy, a specialized non-surgical treatment commonly used for people suffering from chronic lower back pain, sciatica, bulging discs, herniated discs, and certain degenerative spinal conditions.
So how does it work?
The motorized table applies a gentle, controlled pulling force to the lumbar spine (lower back). This creates a process called **decompression**, where the vertebrae are slightly separated, reducing pressure on the spinal discs and nearby nerves.
Why is this important?
🦴 Reduces Disc Pressure
Spinal discs act as shock absorbers between your vertebrae. When a disc bulges or herniates, it can press on nearby nerves and cause pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Decompression may help reduce this pressure.
💧 Improves Nutrient Exchange
Unlike many tissues in the body, spinal discs have a very limited blood supply. The gentle stretching and relaxation cycles help encourage the movement of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, supporting their health and recovery.
